title: Base change of an ell-adic inverse-limit tower and of its finite reduction tensor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a scheme morphism $h:T'\to T$, the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and their inverse-image functor [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Write $R_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$, with constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and coefficient ring [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $(F_{r,T},t_{r,T})_{r\geq1}$ and $(F_{r,T'},t_{r,T'})_{r\geq1}$ be towers of $R_T$- and $R_{T'}$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], respectively, with $\ell^rF_{r,S}=0$. Let $L_S=\varprojlim_r F_{r,S}$ with projections $p_{r,S}$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Assume that the canonical ring-sheaf maps $h^{-1}(\Lambda)_T\to(\Lambda)_{T'}$ of constant sheaves are isomorphisms for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z_\ell$ (and, in the second part, for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^N$ and $A$), and regard inverse images of modules as modules over the target constant rings through them. Suppose $R_{T'}$-linear isomorphisms $\beta_{r,h}:h^{-1}F_{r,T}\to F_{r,T'}$ commute with transitions. Then there is a unique $R_{T'}$-linear map
$$c_h:h^{-1}L_T\to L_{T'},\qquad p_{r,T'}c_h=\beta_{r,h}h^{-1}p_{r,T}.$$
If such tower comparisons are given for identity and composable morphisms and obey their identity/composition laws, the $c_h$ obey the same laws, under the canonical inverse-image composition identifications.

Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbf Z_\ell$-algebra killed by $\ell^N$, $N\geq1$, and let $Q_S=(\mathbf Z/\ell^N)_S$. Form sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], put $B_S=L_S\otimes_{R_S}A_S$ and $D_S=F_{N,S}\otimes_{Q_S}A_S$, and define $\alpha_S:B_S\to D_S$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto p_{N,S}(x)\otimes a$. Under the canonical tensor pullback identifications, $b_h=c_h\otimes1:h^{-1}B_T\to B_{T'}$ and $d_h=\beta_{N,h}\otimes1:h^{-1}D_T\to D_{T'}$ satisfy
$$\alpha_{T'}b_h=d_hh^{-1}\alpha_T.$$
The $b_h$ obey identity and composition laws. If $\alpha_T$ and $\alpha_{T'}$ are isomorphisms, then $b_h$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: For each S, the tower (F_{r,S}, t_{r,S}) is a diagram of sheaves of R_S-modules. By [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], its inverse limit L_S exists in that module category, is computed sectionwise by compatible tuples, and has coordinate projections p_{r,S}. In particular the projections satisfy t_{r,S} p_{r+1,S}=p_{r,S}.

source.place: Lemma 03DB and Lemma 03CO (2), limits of sheaves of modules and sectionwise computation

proof.text: Apply h^{-1} to p_{r,T} and then compose with beta_{r,h}. The resulting maps h^{-1}L_T -> F_{r,T'} are R_{T'}-linear after the stipulated identification h^{-1}R_T ≅ R_{T'}. For every transition, the equality t_{r,T'} beta_{r+1,h}=beta_{r,h} h^{-1}(t_{r,T}) and functoriality of h^{-1} give t_{r,T'} beta_{r+1,h} h^{-1}p_{r+1,T}=beta_{r,h}h^{-1}p_{r,T}, so these maps form a cone over the T' tower.

source.place: Tag 09A5, functoriality of the inverse-image construction on sheaf morphisms

proof.text: The limit universal property in [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] gives a unique morphism c_h:h^{-1}L_T -> L_{T'} whose composite with p_{r,T'} is beta_{r,h} h^{-1}p_{r,T} for every r. The cone maps are R_{T'}-linear, so the induced map is R_{T'}-linear in the sheaf-of-modules category. Uniqueness is tested after all coordinate projections, since the compatible-tuple description makes those projections jointly monic.

source.place: Lemma 03DB and Lemma 03CO (2), limit universal property and coordinate projections

proof.text:
For composable maps $T''\xrightarrow{g}T'\xrightarrow{h}T$, use $(h\circ g)^{-1}\cong g^{-1}h^{-1}$ from [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image]. The defining equations give
$$p_{r,T''}c_g g^{-1}(c_h)=\beta_{r,g}g^{-1}(p_{r,T'}c_h)=\beta_{r,g}g^{-1}(\beta_{r,h})(h\circ g)^{-1}p_{r,T}=\beta_{r,h\circ g}(h\circ g)^{-1}p_{r,T}.$$
The assumed composition equation for $\beta$ gives the last equality. Limit uniqueness [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] implies $c_{h\circ g}=c_g g^{-1}(c_h)$. For the identity map, the assumed identity equation for $\beta$ gives $p_{r,T}c_{\mathrm{id}}=p_{r,T}$, so the same uniqueness gives $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$.

source.place: Final sentence, compatibility with identity and composition of base changes

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] (1) with $\mathcal O=R_T$ to $L_T,A_T$, and with $\mathcal O=Q_T$ to $F_{N,T},A_T$: the isomorphisms $\sigma^h$ give $h^{-1}B_T\cong h^{-1}L_T\otimes_{h^{-1}R_T}h^{-1}A_T$ and $h^{-1}D_T\cong h^{-1}F_{N,T}\otimes_{h^{-1}Q_T}h^{-1}A_T$. Transport these along the stipulated ring isomorphisms $h^{-1}R_T\cong R_{T'}$, $h^{-1}Q_T\cong Q_{T'}$ and $h^{-1}A_T\cong A_{T'}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]; the balancing relations correspond because these maps commute with the coefficient ring homomorphisms $\mathbf Z_\ell\to\mathbf Z/\ell^N\to A$: both composites send each constant section to that same section, so they agree by the defining uniqueness in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. This gives the canonical tensor pullback identifications
$$h^{-1}B_T\cong(h^{-1}L_T)\otimes_{R_{T'}}A_{T'},\qquad h^{-1}D_T\cong(h^{-1}F_{N,T})\otimes_{Q_{T'}}A_{T'},$$
sending $h^{-1}(x\otimes a)$ to $h^{-1}x\otimes a$ and $h^{-1}(y\otimes a)$ to $h^{-1}y\otimes a$ for local sections $x,y$ and constant $a$. Here $\beta_{N,h}$ is $Q_{T'}$-linear, since it is $R_{T'}$-linear and $R_{T'}\to Q_{T'}$ is locally surjective. Postcomposing the first identification with $c_h\otimes1$ defines $b_h$; postcomposing the second with $\beta_{N,h}\otimes1$ defines $d_h$. These maps are supplied by functoriality of the tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, with the pure-tensor description of the comparison

proof.text: First, the formula for $\alpha_S$ is balanced: $p_{N,S}(rx)\otimes a=(\bar r\,p_{N,S}(x))\otimes a=p_{N,S}(x)\otimes ra$, since both $F_{N,S}$ and $A_S$ carry the quotient $Q_S$-action. Hence $\alpha_S=\pi_S\circ(p_{N,S}\otimes1)$, where $p_{N,S}\otimes1:L_S\otimes_{R_S}A_S\to F_{N,S}\otimes_{R_S}A_S$ is the tensor map [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and $\pi_S:F_{N,S}\otimes_{R_S}A_S\to F_{N,S}\otimes_{Q_S}A_S$ sends $y\otimes a$ to $y\otimes a$. By naturality in [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] (1) applied to $p_{N,T}$, and by its change-of-rings clause (2) for $R_T\to Q_T$, the identifications of Step 5 carry $h^{-1}\alpha_T$ to the map $h^{-1}x\otimes a\mapsto h^{-1}p_{N,T}(x)\otimes a$, and then $d_hh^{-1}\alpha_T$ sends $h^{-1}x\otimes a$ to $\beta_{N,h}(h^{-1}p_{N,T}(x))\otimes a$. Along the other route, $\alpha_{T'}b_h$ sends it to $p_{N,T'}(c_h(h^{-1}x))\otimes a$, which is the same element by Step 3. The elements $h^{-1}x\otimes a$, for $x$ a section of $L_T$ over some $V$ and $a$ constant, generate $(h^{-1}L_T)\otimes_{R_{T'}}A_{T'}$ locally (the sections of an inverse image are locally restrictions of such $h^{-1}x$, and the sheaf tensor is locally generated by pure tensors), so the two module maps agree. This proves $\alpha_{T'}b_h=d_hh^{-1}\alpha_T$.

source.place: Final sentence, compatibility of the inverse-limit projection with the finite tensor square

proof.text: Use the composition isomorphism $\gamma:(h\circ g)^{-1}\cong g^{-1}h^{-1}$ and the coherence clause (3) of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison], whose $\gamma$ is the identification of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] used in Step 4. For $T''\xrightarrow{g}T'\xrightarrow{h}T$, clause (3) shows that the tensor pullback identification for $h\circ g$ is the composite of $g^{-1}$ of that for $h$ with that for $g$, so the two routes $b_g g^{-1}(b_h)$ and $b_{h\circ g}$ are $(c_g\,g^{-1}(c_h))\otimes1$ and $c_{h\circ g}\otimes1$ after the same identification. These are equal by Step 4. The coefficient comparisons agree because their composites send each constant section $a$ to itself, as in Step 5. The identity clause of (3) and $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ give $b_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. Functoriality of the tensor construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives these equations as sheaf maps.

source.place: Final sentence, compatibility with composition after tensoring

proof.text: If $\alpha_T$ and $\alpha_{T'}$ are isomorphisms, then $d_h$ is an isomorphism: it is the composite of the isomorphism $\sigma^h$ of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] (1) (transported along the coefficient ring isomorphisms) with $\beta_{N,h}\otimes1$, and tensoring $\beta_{N,h}^{-1}$ with $1$ gives an inverse to $\beta_{N,h}\otimes1$. The inverse image of $\alpha_T$ is an isomorphism because a functor sends an inverse pair to an inverse pair. The commutative square therefore rewrites $b_h=\alpha_{T'}^{-1}d_hh^{-1}(\alpha_T)$, a composite of isomorphisms, so $b_h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Final sentence, isomorphism conclusion from the commuting tensor square

lean.statement: theorem tateInverseLimitBaseChange (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] {T T' : Scheme.{u}} (h : T' ⟶ T) [IsIso (proEtaleCoefficientInverseImageMap h (ULift.{u} (PadicInt l)))] (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ tateModules T (ULift.{u} (PadicInt l))) (F' : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ tateModules T' (ULift.{u} (PadicInt l))) (hF : TateTowerKilled l F) (hF' : TateTowerKilled l F') (β : F ⋙ tatePullback h (ULift.{u} (PadicInt l)) ≅ F') : (∀ r : ℕ, tateLimitMap h _ F F' β ≫ limit.π F' (op r) = (tatePullback h _).map (limit.π F (op r)) ≫ β.hom.app (op r)) ∧ ∀ c : (tatePullback h _).obj (limit F) ⟶ limit F', (∀ r : ℕ, c ≫ limit.π F' (op r) = (tatePullback h _).map (limit.π F (op r)) ≫ β.hom.app (op r)) → c = tateLimitMap h _ F F' β
